title: Universal Bounds On Entropy Production From Fluctuating Coarse-grained Trajectories
authors: Udo Seifert
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 20 July 2026;
tldr: This review presents universal lower bounds on entropy production derived from coarse-grained trajectories in stochastic thermodynamics, applicable to both steady and time-dependent regimes.
motivation: Entropy production is central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics but is often difficult to measure in partially observed systems, motivating the need for model-free bounds from accessible observables.
method: The paper reviews stochastic thermodynamics approaches that infer entropy production bounds from coarse-grained observables such as states, currents, correlations, and waiting times, without requiring full microscopic knowledge.
result: It highlights universal bounds that hold across various regimes and discusses progress in trajectory-level estimation, providing a unified framework for inferring dissipation from partial information.
conclusion: The review consolidates recent advances in bounding entropy production from coarse-grained data, offering practical tools for quantifying non-equilibrium behavior in complex systems.

title: Quantum Secret Sharing In A Triangular Superconducting Quantum Network
authors: Haoxiong Yan
Allen Zang
Joel Grebel
Xuntao Wu
Ming-Han Chou
Gustav Andersson
Christopher R. Conner
Yash J. Joshi
Shiheng Li
Jacob M. Miller
Rhys G. Povey
Hong Qiao
Eric Chitambar
Andrew N. Cleland
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 August 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates quantum secret sharing in a triangular superconducting quantum network, a key multi-party quantum communication protocol.
motivation: Quantum secret sharing is a fundamental multi-party quantum communication task, and demonstrating it in a superconducting quantum network is a significant step towards practical quantum networks.
method: The authors implement a triangular network of three superconducting qubits and use entanglement to distribute a secret among three parties, with any two able to reconstruct it.
result: They successfully demonstrate the protocol, achieving high fidelity and showing the feasibility of quantum secret sharing in a superconducting platform.
conclusion: This work advances quantum network capabilities by showcasing a multi-party protocol on a scalable platform, contributing to the development of practical quantum networks.

title: Merging-based Quantum Repeater
authors: Maria Flors Mor-Ruiz
Jorge Miguel-Ramiro
Julius Wallnöfer
Tim Coopmans
Wolfgang Dür
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 05 August 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a novel quantum repeater architecture based on merging operations, potentially improving entanglement distribution efficiency.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing schemes face limitations in resource overhead and performance. The authors aim to introduce a new repeater design that leverages merging operations to enhance entanglement distribution.
method: The paper likely presents a theoretical framework for a merging-based quantum repeater, possibly involving entanglement swapping, purification, and merging of quantum states. It may include simulations or analytical models to evaluate performance.
result: The proposed merging-based repeater demonstrates improved performance metrics such as higher entanglement generation rates or lower resource requirements compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: The merging-based quantum repeater offers a promising alternative for scalable quantum networks, potentially enabling more efficient long-distance quantum communication.

title: Tight Bounds On Recurrence Time In Closed Quantum Systems
authors: Marcin Kotowski And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Kotowski and Michał Oszmaniec

The evolution of an isolated quantum system inevitably exhibits recurrence: the state returns to the vicinity of its initial condition after finite time. Despite its fundamental nature, a rigorous quantitative understanding of recurrence has been lacking. We establish upper bounds on the recurrence …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060402] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes tight upper bounds on the recurrence time of closed quantum systems, providing a rigorous quantitative understanding of a fundamental phenomenon.
motivation: Recurrence is a fundamental property of isolated quantum systems, but a rigorous quantitative understanding has been lacking. The authors aim to fill this gap by deriving tight bounds.
method: The authors use mathematical techniques from quantum information theory, likely involving operator norms, spectral analysis, and perhaps entropy measures, to derive upper bounds on recurrence time.
result: They establish tight upper bounds on the recurrence time, improving upon previous results and providing a rigorous quantitative characterization.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of quantum dynamics and has implications for quantum information processing, such as in quantum control and thermalization.

title: Robust Device-independent Characterization Of Sharpness And Incompatibility Of Unsharp Instruments
authors: Qian Zhang, Kai-Yu Yuan, Yan-Xin Rong, Zhen Shang, Yong-Jian Gu, And Ya Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Zhang, Kai-Yu Yuan, Yan-Xin Rong, Zhen Shang, Yong-Jian Gu, and Ya Xiao

The authors present a device-independent protocol for characterizing unsharp quantum instruments using an entanglement‑assisted code with restricted classical communication between two parties. They experimentally demonstrate the predicted enhancement in decoding probability by implementing tunable unsharp measurements with a Mach-Zehnder interferometer.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022411] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a device-independent protocol to characterize unsharp quantum instruments, demonstrating enhanced decoding probability via tunable unsharp measurements in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer.
motivation: Characterizing unsharp measurements and their incompatibility in a device-independent manner is crucial for quantum information protocols, yet remains challenging.
method: The authors propose an entanglement-assisted code with restricted classical communication between two parties, and experimentally implement tunable unsharp measurements using a Mach-Zehnder interferometer.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the predicted enhancement in decoding probability, validating the device-independent characterization.
conclusion: The work provides a robust method for characterizing unsharp instruments, advancing device-independent quantum information processing.

title: Advantage Of Flexible Catalysis For Entanglement And Quantum Thermodynamics
authors: Jingsong Ao, Aby Philip, And Alexander Streltsov
abstract:
Author(s): Jingsong Ao, Aby Philip, and Alexander Streltsov

Understanding the fundamental limits of state convertibility is crucial for establishing the boundaries of quantum information processing and thermodynamic efficiency. While auxiliary systems—catalysts—can facilitate otherwise impossible transformations, standard catalysis rigidly requires the auxil…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022407] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces flexible catalysts that can be used up to a certain extent, expanding the set of achievable state transformations in entanglement theory and quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Standard catalysis in quantum resource theories requires the catalyst to be returned exactly unchanged, which limits the range of possible transformations. The authors aim to relax this constraint to enable more transformations while still providing an advantage.
method: They formalize the concept of flexible catalysts, allowing partial consumption or alteration of the catalyst, and derive conditions for when such catalysts enable otherwise impossible transformations. They apply this to entanglement theory and quantum thermodynamics.
result: Flexible catalysis is shown to provide an advantage over standard catalysis, enabling a broader class of state transformations in both entanglement and thermodynamic settings. They characterize the conditions and quantify the advantage.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of catalytic transformations in quantum information, suggesting that flexible catalysts are a powerful tool for state conversion, with implications for quantum resource theories.

title: Probing An Electron-spin Ensemble With Squeezed Microwave Signals
authors: P. Oehrl, F. Fesquet, K. E. Honasoge, M. Handschuh, A. Marx, R. Gross, K. G. Fedorov, And H. Huebl
abstract:
Author(s): P. Oehrl, F. Fesquet, K. E. Honasoge, M. Handschuh, A. Marx, R. Gross, K. G. Fedorov, and H. Huebl

The efficient transfer of quantum states into a long-lived storage unit such as solid-state spin ensembles is widely recognized as a critical challenge with significant implications for quantum communication, sensing, and computing applications. Here, we experimentally investigate the interaction of…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022603] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes an electron-spin ensemble using squeezed microwave signals, demonstrating enhanced sensitivity and characterizing the spin ensemble's interaction with the squeezed field.
motivation: Efficient transfer of quantum states into long-lived solid-state spin ensembles is critical for quantum communication, sensing, and computing. Probing such ensembles with squeezed light can improve measurement sensitivity and enable quantum-enhanced sensing.
method: The authors use a superconducting resonator coupled to an electron-spin ensemble (likely NV centers or similar) and apply squeezed microwave signals to probe the ensemble. They measure the reflected/transmitted signals to extract information about the spin ensemble's properties and its coupling to the resonator.
result: The experiment demonstrates that squeezed microwave signals can probe the spin ensemble with reduced noise, leading to improved sensitivity in characterizing the ensemble. The results show the potential of using squeezed fields for quantum-enhanced metrology with spin ensembles.
conclusion: The work establishes a platform for quantum-enhanced sensing and quantum state transfer using spin ensembles coupled to superconducting circuits, relevant for hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.

title: Scalable Repeater Architecture For Long-range Quantum Energy Teleportation In Gapped Systems
authors: M. Y. Abd-Rabbou, Irfan Siddique, Saeed Haddadi, And Cong-Feng Qiao
abstract:
Author(s): M. Y. Abd-Rabbou, Irfan Siddique, Saeed Haddadi, and Cong-Feng Qiao

Quantum Energy Teleportation (QET) is a protocol in which a remote measurement activates locally inaccessible ergotropy stored in the ground state of a many-body system by consuming preexisting entanglement and a classical communication channel. Nevertheless, the implementation of QET is severely im…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022601] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scalable repeater architecture for quantum energy teleportation in gapped systems, addressing the practical limitation of exponential decay of teleported energy with distance.
motivation: Quantum energy teleportation (QET) is limited by the exponential decay of teleported energy over distance, hindering long-range applications. The authors aim to overcome this by designing a repeater architecture that enables scalable energy transfer.
method: The authors introduce a repeater protocol that divides the long-distance channel into segments, each with its own entangled resource, and uses local operations and classical communication to sequentially teleport energy across the chain. They analyze the performance in terms of teleported energy and entanglement consumption.
result: The proposed architecture achieves a polynomial scaling of teleported energy with distance, in contrast to the exponential decay in direct QET, while maintaining a finite entanglement cost per segment.
conclusion: The work provides a practical pathway for long-range quantum energy teleportation, with potential applications in quantum batteries and energy distribution in quantum networks.

title: Quantum Geometric Tensor Determines The Pure-State I.i.d. Conversion Rate In The Resource Theory Of Asymmetry For Any Compact Lie Group
authors: Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, And Hiroyasu Tajima
abstract:
Author(s): Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, and Hiroyasu Tajima

Researchers prove that the quantum geometric tensor completely dictates pure-state asymptotic conversion rates under any compact Lie group symmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031028] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the quantum geometric tensor fully determines the asymptotic conversion rate of pure states under any compact Lie group symmetry in the resource theory of asymmetry.
motivation: The resource theory of asymmetry is fundamental for quantum information, and determining conversion rates is a key problem. The quantum geometric tensor is a natural quantity that may capture the relevant constraints.
method: The authors provide a rigorous proof that the quantum geometric tensor completely dictates the pure-state i.i.d. conversion rate under any compact Lie group symmetry, using techniques from quantum information and group theory.
result: They establish a direct connection between the quantum geometric tensor and the asymptotic conversion rate, showing that the tensor is the sole determinant of the rate.
conclusion: This result provides a complete characterization of pure-state conversion in asymmetry resource theory, advancing the understanding of quantum resources and their manipulation.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment-like technique, achieving robust entanglement despite imperfections.
motivation: Remote entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but maintaining it in the presence of noise and imperfections is challenging. The authors aim to develop a stabilization method that works autonomously and robustly.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two remote nodes are coupled via a unidirectional channel, and use a feedback-based stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment to continuously correct errors and maintain entanglement.
result: They achieve stable remote entanglement with high fidelity, demonstrating resilience to realistic imperfections such as loss and noise, and show that the stabilization is autonomous (no active measurement or feedforward).
conclusion: The work provides a practical and scalable approach for maintaining remote entanglement in quantum networks, advancing the feasibility of distributed quantum information processing.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully autonomous method to entangle two spatially separated superconducting qubits via a shared nonlocal squeezed microwave reservoir, offering a robust platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in quantum networks.
motivation: Entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks, but current methods often require active control or suffer from low rates. This work aims to provide a simpler, autonomous approach using a squeezed reservoir.
method: Two superconducting qubits are coupled to a common microwave resonator that is squeezed, creating a nonlocal quantum-correlated reservoir. The qubits interact with this reservoir, and the dissipative dynamics autonomously drive them into an entangled steady state.
result: The authors experimentally demonstrate the generation of stationary entanglement between the two qubits, with the entanglement persisting as long as the squeezing is maintained. The scheme is robust and does not require active feedback or measurement.
conclusion: This work establishes a new platform for autonomous entanglement distribution, which could be integrated into future quantum networks to improve scalability and efficiency.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel scheme for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian phases, avoiding the need for braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D typically relies on braiding anyons, which is complex. The authors aim to simplify this by using non-Abelian phases without braiding.
method: They propose a method that temporarily moves data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform logic gates, leveraging the properties of these phases for computation.
result: The scheme enables universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D without the need for braiding, potentially simplifying experimental implementation.
conclusion: This work provides a new pathway for large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation, with implications for quantum error correction and topological quantum computing.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity of tin-vacancy centers in diamond photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement generation for quantum networks.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity entanglement generation in scalable quantum networks, it is crucial to have quantum emitters with strong light-matter interaction, quantified by coherent cooperativity above unity.
method: The authors coupled individual tin-vacancy (SnV) centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities in diamond and characterized the optical properties, measuring the coherent cooperativity.
result: They achieved above-unity coherent cooperativity, indicating strong coupling between the SnV centers and cavity photons, which is a key milestone for efficient spin-photon interfaces.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a promising platform for quantum networking applications, as the high cooperativity enables high-fidelity entanglement generation and paves the way for scalable quantum networks.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously considered classical.
motivation: To provide a unified criterion for quantumness that recovers standard signatures and uncovers nonclassicality in processes thought to be classical, potentially enabling new quantum technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process theories and generalized probabilistic theories, defining a boundary between classical and nonclassical processes and applying it to various examples.
result: The rule recovers many known quantum signatures and identifies hidden quantum features in processes like certain classical stochastic processes, suggesting broader applicability of quantum resources.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of quantum-classical boundary and may have implications for quantum information processing and resource theories.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Fast and high-fidelity qubit readout is crucial for scalable quantum computing, and Purcell filtering is often needed to protect qubits during measurement. The authors aim to simplify this by integrating Purcell protection directly into the readout mechanism.
method: They propose a novel transmon readout scheme that exploits nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling between the qubit and a readout resonator, which provides strong dispersive readout while naturally suppressing Purcell decay.
result: The architecture demonstrates fast readout with high fidelity and intrinsic Purcell protection, as shown through theoretical analysis and experimental validation.
conclusion: This work offers a promising approach to simplify transmon readout while improving performance, potentially benefiting scalable quantum processors.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, offering new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Single-shot error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, and existing codes may not support exotic topological orders. The authors aim to extend single-shot capabilities to fermionic and chiral phases.
method: They construct a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes, likely based on color codes, and analyze their error correction properties, demonstrating single-shot decoding for the desired topological orders.
result: The proposed codes achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, which is a novel contribution to quantum error correction.
conclusion: This work introduces new code families that could enable fault-tolerant quantum computation with exotic topological orders, advancing the field of quantum error correction.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires high overhead in qubits and time. The goal is to reduce these overheads using advanced quantum error correction codes.
method: The authors employ good quantum LDPC codes and introduce parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
result: The proposed scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, significantly improving the efficiency of fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that good quantum LDPC codes can enable practical fault-tolerant quantum computation with reduced resource requirements, advancing the field of quantum error correction.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to certify the impossibility of simulating non-projective measurements by projective ones, with experimental validation on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are limited. The authors aim to provide a robust and complete framework for such certification.
method: They develop a new complete SDP hierarchy that characterizes the set of measurements simulable by projective measurements, and apply it to certify non-projective measurements. They also perform an experiment on a trapped-ion system to demonstrate the certification.
result: The hierarchy provides a rigorous and complete method for certifying non-projective measurements, and the experimental results confirm the theoretical predictions, showing the practical applicability.
conclusion: The work advances the certification of quantum measurements, offering a powerful tool for quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, quantifying the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum detectors and for fundamental limits in quantum measurement. The authors aim to provide a minimal model that captures the essential trade-offs.
method: The authors develop a minimal quantum-particle-detector model and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics, likely using master equations or stochastic thermodynamics to compute entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: The model demonstrates a fundamental trade-off between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing quantitative insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition in quantum detectors.
conclusion: The findings establish fundamental thermodynamic bounds on quantum measurement, with implications for the design of autonomous quantum devices and the understanding of information-thermodynamics links.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin ensembles that enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement, demonstrating experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Heterogeneous solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum information processing but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and individual addressability challenges, limiting scalability.
method: The authors propose a programmable control framework that leverages global driving and optical heralding to entangle spins in inhomogeneous ensembles, with techniques to mitigate disorder and enable scalable operations.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with experimental overhead projected for 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum information processing using inhomogeneous spin ensembles, relevant for hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits with random measurements, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and introducing logical measurement statistics for stability analysis.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction and the stability of quantum codes under monitored dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits, focusing on the effect of random measurements on code properties, and introduce new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
result: They demonstrate that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, providing a new perspective on the interplay between measurements and quantum error correction.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of monitored quantum dynamics and may inform the design of more robust quantum error correction protocols.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chipset for self-testing quantum random number generation, advancing practical device-independent quantum cryptography.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide certified randomness without trusting devices, but current implementations are bulky and impractical. The authors aim to miniaturize this technology for production-scale quantum security devices.
method: They design and fabricate a silicon photonic chipset that implements a self-testing QRNG protocol, integrating the necessary photonic components for generating and measuring quantum states, and perform a self-testing analysis to certify randomness.
result: The chipset successfully generates certified random numbers, demonstrating the feasibility of compact, integrated self-testing QRNGs. The implementation achieves high-speed randomness generation with device-independent security guarantees.
conclusion: This work paves the way for practical, miniaturized quantum security devices, making self-testing randomness expansion accessible for real-world applications.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric geometries for quantum tree codes, enhancing quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but current tree-code schemes are resource-intensive and challenging to implement. The authors aim to improve efficiency and practicality.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for quantum tree codes and introduce optimized asymmetric code geometries, likely through theoretical analysis and simulations.
result: The combined approach boosts quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility, reducing resource requirements.
conclusion: The proposed hierarchical generation and asymmetric tree codes offer a more resource-efficient path for quantum repeaters, advancing practical quantum networks.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and implementations.
motivation: To provide an up-to-date overview of continuous-variable (CV) quantum communication, highlighting its advantages over discrete-variable approaches and its maturity.
method: The paper is a review article that synthesizes the state of the art in CV quantum communication, including theoretical foundations, protocol designs, security proofs, and experimental demonstrations.
result: The review consolidates key developments in CV-QKD, quantum repeaters, and other CV quantum networking protocols, emphasizing their practical feasibility and security.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and promising approach for practical quantum networks, with distinct advantages in implementation and integration with existing telecom infrastructure.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a systematic classification and analysis of quantum cryptography beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a structured overview of available primitives and their practical implementations.
method: The authors review and classify various quantum cryptographic primitives, discussing their security definitions, theoretical capabilities, limitations, and current photonic experimental implementations.
result: The review presents a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic protocols, highlights their security guarantees and limitations, and surveys experimental progress in photonic platforms.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, with promising theoretical foundations and emerging experimental demonstrations, though practical challenges remain.

title: Quantifiers And Witnesses For The Nonclassicality Of Measurements And Of States
authors: Yujie Zhang, Yìlè Yīng, And David Schmid
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2180 (2026).

In recent work [Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050], we proposed a unified notion of nonclassicality that applies to arbitrary processes in quantum theory, including individual quantum states, measurements, and sets thereof. This notion is derived from the principle of generalized noncontextuality, but in a novel manner that applies to individual processes rather than full experiments or theories. In the present work, we develop semidefinite-programming-based certificates and witnesses for the nonclassicality of states, sources, measurements, and sets thereof. These theory-dependent methods complement theory-independent approaches based on noncontextuality inequalities. We demonstrate the framework through a variety of explicit examples.

.
tldr: This paper develops semidefinite-programming-based certificates and witnesses for the nonclassicality of quantum states, measurements, and sets thereof, based on generalized noncontextuality.
motivation: To provide practical tools for detecting nonclassicality in individual quantum processes, complementing theory-independent noncontextuality inequalities.
method: The authors formulate semidefinite programs that serve as certificates and witnesses for nonclassicality, applicable to states, sources, measurements, and sets, and demonstrate them with examples.
result: They present explicit SDP-based methods that can certify nonclassicality in various scenarios, as illustrated through examples.
conclusion: The framework offers a versatile and computationally efficient approach to witness nonclassicality, advancing the study of quantum contextuality and its applications.

title: Stabilizer Ranks, Barnes Wall Lattices And Magic Monotones
authors: Amolak Ratan Kalra And Pulkit Sinha
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2179 (2026).

In 2024, Kliuchnikov and Schönnenbeck showed a connection between the Barnes Wall lattices, stabilizer states and Clifford operations. In this work, we study their results and relate them to the problem of lower bounding stabilizer ranks. We show the first quantitative lower bound on stabilizer fidelity as a function of stabilizer ranks, which reproduces the linear-by-log lower bound for [MATH], i.e, on the approximate stabilizer rank of [MATH]. In fact, we show that the lower bound holds even when the fidelity between the approximation and [MATH] is exponentially small, which is currently the best lower bound in this regime. Next, we define a new magic monotone for pure states, the Barnes Wall norm, and its corresponding approximate variant. We upper bound these monotones by the [MATH]-count of state preparation, and also by the stabilizer ranks. In particular, the upper bound given by the [MATH]-count is tight, in the sense that we exhibit states that achieve the bound. Apart from these results, we give a Fidelity Amplification algorithm, which provides a trade-off between approximation error and the stabilizer rank. As a corollary, it gives us a way to compose approximate stabilizer decompositions into approximate decompositions of their tensor products. Finally, we provide an alternate, elementary proof of the existence and density of product states with maximal stabilizer ranks, which was first proven by Lovitz and Steffan (2022), where they used results from algebraic geometry.

.
tldr: This paper connects Barnes Wall lattices to stabilizer ranks, providing new lower bounds and a magic monotone.
motivation: To understand and improve bounds on stabilizer ranks, which are crucial for quantum resource theories and magic state distillation.
method: The authors study the connection between Barnes Wall lattices and stabilizer states, derive quantitative lower bounds on stabilizer fidelity, define a new magic monotone (Barnes Wall norm), and provide a fidelity amplification algorithm.
result: They obtain the first quantitative lower bound on stabilizer fidelity as a function of stabilizer ranks, which is best in the exponentially small fidelity regime, and show tight upper bounds for the new monotone via T-count.
conclusion: The work advances the resource theory of magic states by providing new tools and bounds, with potential applications in quantum computing and cryptography.

title: A Complete Theory Of The Clifford Commutant
authors: Lennart Bittel, Jens Eisert, Lorenzo Leone, Antonio A. Mele, And Salvatore F.E. Oliviero
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2171 (2026).

The Clifford group plays a central role in quantum information science. It is the building block for many error-correcting schemes and matches the first three moments of the Haar measure over the unitary group-a property that is essential for a broad range of quantum algorithms, with applications in pseudorandomness, learning theory, benchmarking, and entanglement distillation. At the heart of understanding many properties of the Clifford group lies the Clifford commutant: the set of operators that commute with [MATH]-fold tensor powers of Clifford unitaries. Previous understanding of this commutant has been limited to relatively small values of [MATH], constrained by the number of qubits [MATH]. In this work, we develop a complete theory of the Clifford commutant. Our first result provides an explicit orthogonal basis for the commutant and computes its dimension for arbitrary [MATH] and [MATH]. We also introduce an alternative and easy-to-manipulate basis formed by isotropic sums of Pauli operators. We show that this basis is generated by products of permutations, which generate the unitary group commutant, and at most three other operators. Additionally, we develop a graphical calculus allowing a diagrammatic manipulation of elements of this basis. These results enable a wealth of applications: among others, we characterize all measurable magic measures and identify optimal strategies for stabilizer property testing, whose success probability also offers an operational interpretation to stabilizer entropies. Finally, we show that these results also generalize to multi-qudit systems with prime local dimension.

.
tldr: This paper provides a complete theory of the Clifford commutant, offering explicit bases and a graphical calculus, with applications to magic measures and stabilizer property testing.
motivation: The Clifford group is central to quantum information, but the structure of its commutant was only partially understood for small tensor powers. A complete characterization is needed for many applications.
method: The authors derive an explicit orthogonal basis for the Clifford commutant for arbitrary tensor power and qubit number, introduce an alternative basis of isotropic sums of Pauli operators, and develop a graphical calculus for diagrammatic manipulation.
result: They compute the dimension of the commutant, show the basis is generated by permutations and at most three other operators, and apply the results to characterize measurable magic measures and identify optimal strategies for stabilizer property testing.
conclusion: The complete theory of the Clifford commutant enables a wealth of applications in quantum information, including magic quantification and property testing, and extends to multi-qudit systems with prime local dimension.

title: Fast Quantum Measurement Tomography With Optimal Error Bounds
authors: Leonardo Zambrano, Sergi Ramos-Calderer, And Richard Kueng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2162 (2026).

We present a two-step protocol for quantum measurement tomography that is light on classical co-processing cost and still achieves optimal sample complexity. Given measurement data from a known probe state ensemble, we first apply least-squares estimation to produce an unconstrained approximation of the POVM, and then project this estimate onto the set of valid quantum measurements. For a POVM with [MATH] outcomes acting on a [MATH]-dimensional system, we show that the protocol requires [MATH] samples to achieve error [MATH] in worst-case distance, and [MATH] samples in average-case distance. We further establish two matching sample complexity lower bounds of [MATH] and [MATH] for any non-adaptive, single-copy POVM tomography protocol. Hence, our projected least squares POVM tomography is sample-optimal in both the dimension and the number of outcomes for both distances. Our method admits an analytic form when using global or local 2-designs as probe ensembles and enables rigorous non-asymptotic error guarantees. Finally, we also complement our findings with empirical performance studies carried out on a noisy superconducting quantum computer with flux-tunable transmon qubits.

.
tldr: This paper presents a sample-optimal two-step protocol for quantum measurement tomography using projected least squares, with rigorous error bounds and experimental validation on a superconducting quantum computer.
motivation: Quantum measurement tomography is essential for characterizing quantum devices, but existing protocols often have suboptimal sample complexity or high classical processing cost. The authors aim to design a protocol that is both sample-optimal and computationally efficient.
method: The protocol first applies least-squares estimation to measurement data from a known probe ensemble to obtain an unconstrained POVM approximation, then projects this estimate onto the set of valid quantum measurements. They analyze sample complexity for worst-case and average-case distances, and prove matching lower bounds for any non-adaptive single-copy protocol.
result: The protocol achieves optimal sample complexity in both dimension and number of outcomes for both distances, with analytic forms for global and local 2-designs. They also demonstrate empirical performance on a noisy superconducting quantum computer.
conclusion: The proposed projected least squares method is sample-optimal and practical, providing a rigorous and efficient solution for quantum measurement tomography, with potential applications in quantum device characterization and quantum information processing.

title: Towards Unconditional Uncloneable Encryption
authors: Pierre Botteron, Anne Broadbent, Eric Culf, Ion Nechita, Clément Pellegrini, And Denis Rochette
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2157 (2026).

Uncloneable encryption is a cryptographic primitive which encrypts a classical message into a quantum ciphertext, such that two quantum adversaries are limited in their capacity of being able to simultaneously decrypt, given the key and quantum side-information produced from the ciphertext. Since its initial proposal and scheme in the random oracle model by Broadbent and Lord [TQC 2020], uncloneable encryption has developed into an important primitive at the foundation of quantum uncloneability for cryptographic primitives. Despite sustained efforts, however, the question of unconditional uncloneable encryption (and in particular of the simplest case, called an uncloneable bit) has remained elusive. Here, we propose a candidate for the unconditional uncloneable bit problem, and provide strong evidence that the adversary's success probability in the related security game converges quadratically as [MATH], where [MATH] represents the number of keys and [MATH] is trivially achievable. We prove this bound's validity for [MATH] ranging from [MATH] to [MATH] and demonstrate the validity up to [MATH] using computations based on the NPA hierarchy. We furthemore provide compelling heuristic evidence towards the general case. In addition, we prove an asymptotic upper bound of [MATH] and give a numerical upper bound of [MATH], which to our knowledge is the best-known value in the unconditional model.

.
tldr: This paper proposes a candidate for unconditional uncloneable encryption and provides strong evidence for its security, with quadratic convergence of adversary success probability.
motivation: Uncloneable encryption is a fundamental primitive in quantum cryptography, but unconditional security (without random oracles) has remained elusive. The authors aim to resolve the simplest case, the uncloneable bit.
method: They propose a specific scheme and analyze its security using the NPA hierarchy and other techniques, proving bounds for certain parameter ranges and providing numerical evidence for others.
result: They prove a quadratic convergence bound for the adversary's success probability for a range of key numbers, and provide an asymptotic upper bound and a numerical upper bound that is the best known in the unconditional model.
conclusion: The work provides strong evidence for the feasibility of unconditional uncloneable encryption, advancing the theoretical foundations of quantum cryptography.

method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to define and measure state complexity in adaptive quantum circuits, likely using complexity measures and circuit analysis.
result: They provide a characterization of state complexity, possibly showing how it scales with circuit parameters and identifying regimes of high complexity.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of quantum state complexity, with implications for quantum advantage and resource estimation.

motivation: High-fidelity quantum gates are essential for scalable quantum computation, but fast gates suffer from waveform distortions that break time-reflection symmetry, limiting fidelity. The authors aim to overcome this trade-off.
method: They propose a cyclic control scheme that restores the symmetry of the control pulses, enabling precise closure of cyclic evolution even at short durations. The method is applied to CZ gates in superconducting qubits.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity CZ gates at speeds previously unattainable, demonstrating improved fidelity compared to conventional symmetric protocols.
conclusion: Cyclic control provides a practical solution to the speed-fidelity trade-off, advancing fast and high-fidelity quantum gates for scalable quantum computation.

tldr: This paper introduces an analytical single-period Floquet protocol for constructing bosonic codes, avoiding slow adiabatic ramps and enabling fast, fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Existing Floquet protocols for bosonic codes require thousands of driving periods due to adiabatic ramps, which is inefficient. The authors aim to circumvent this bottleneck by designing a single-period protocol.
method: The authors propose an analytical construction of a single-period Floquet drive using quantum lattice gates, which directly generates the desired bosonic code without adiabatic evolution.
result: The protocol achieves fast and efficient generation of bosonic codes, significantly reducing the number of driving periods compared to previous methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient approach to bosonic code construction, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

method: The authors propose an explicit N-qubit protocol using one-axis-twisted spin-squeezed states and analyze its performance using quantum Fisher information and Bayesian estimation techniques.
result: The protocol achieves precision that asymptotically matches the fundamental quantum metrological bounds for joint estimation of phase and dephasing strength.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that spin-squeezed states are a practical resource for multiparameter quantum estimation, with implications for quantum sensing and metrology.

method: The authors work under minimal constraints on the Wigner function and derive analytical upper bounds on the purity of states that would verify the conjecture.
result: They obtain upper bounds on purity for Wigner non-negative states that satisfy the conjecture, providing partial progress toward proving the conjecture.
conclusion: The results support the conjecture and offer new tools for studying Wigner entropy, with implications for quantum information theory.

motivation: To achieve optimal precision in multiparameter estimation problems with symmetry, which is a fundamental task in quantum information and metrology.
method: Introduces quantum metrology conditions analogous to quantum error correction, and uses them to construct optimal probe states and measurement schemes for symmetric generators.
result: Provides a systematic strategy for obtaining optimal probe states and measurements, potentially improving precision limits in multiparameter estimation.
conclusion: The framework advances quantum metrology by leveraging quantum error correction concepts, offering practical benefits for quantum sensing and information processing.

motivation: Active systems exhibit phase separation phenomena not captured by equilibrium theories, and a quantitative macroscopic theory is needed.
method: The authors derive a macroscopic Cahn-Hilliard-type equation from microscopic dynamics, incorporating gradient terms and interfacial properties.
result: They obtain predictions for binodal densities, capillary waves, and Ostwald processes, showing three distinct interfacial tensions.
conclusion: The theory provides a quantitative framework for nonequilibrium phase separation, advancing understanding of active matter thermodynamics.

motivation: Most natural systems operate far from equilibrium, yet general principles governing how nonequilibrium driving reshapes distributions and breaks symmetries remain unclear. The authors aim to fill this gap by studying the role of conservative dissipation.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on stochastic thermodynamics, analyzing how conservative forces (dissipative contributions) affect the stationary distribution and symmetry properties of nonequilibrium systems.
result: They show that conservative dissipation can break symmetries that are present in equilibrium, leading to new nonequilibrium stationary states with persistent currents and altered probability distributions.
conclusion: The work provides a general principle for symmetry breaking in nonequilibrium systems, advancing the understanding of information thermodynamics and the role of dissipation in shaping stationary states.

method: The method combines polynomial phase gates with on-demand noise biasing to implement non-Clifford gates in a fault-tolerant manner, likely using a combination of Gaussian operations and non-Gaussian elements.

[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian states needed to represent a given state, and analyze its properties and operational interpretations.
result: They show that the symplectic rank provides a unified measure that dictates the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement, and they compute it for various examples.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a promising tool for characterizing non-Gaussianity and has implications for resource theories and quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

title: Modulator-Assisted Zeno Control Of Energy Transfer In Quantum Batteries
authors: Songbo Xie, Manas Sajjan, Ashok Ajoy, And Sabre Kais
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2178 (2026).

Efficient operation of quantum batteries requires not only fast energy transfer but also the ability to halt the charging process to prevent reverse flow. Existing approaches typically rely on direct control of the charger-battery interaction, which can be experimentally demanding. Here we propose a modulator-assisted quantum battery protocol that enables indirect control of energy transfer while keeping the interaction always on. By applying repeated local unitary operations to an auxiliary modulator qubit, we exploit a Zeno-like mechanism to dynamically reshape the effective Hamiltonian and switch the charger-battery coupling on and off. We demonstrate this mechanism in a minimal three-body model and show that it remains effective beyond the ideal fast-control limit. We further extend the protocol to a collective many-body architecture, where it preserves the characteristic enhancement of charging power, scaling as [MATH] with the number of battery units. We also discuss a possible implementation in an NV-[MATH]C spin platform. Our results establish modulator-assisted Zeno control as a scalable route to regulating energy transfer in quantum batteries.

.
tldr: This paper proposes a modulator-assisted Zeno control protocol for quantum batteries, enabling indirect on/off switching of energy transfer while keeping the interaction always on.
motivation: Efficient quantum battery operation requires halting charging to prevent reverse flow, but direct control of the charger-battery interaction is experimentally demanding. The authors aim to achieve indirect control via a modulator qubit.
method: They apply repeated local unitary operations to an auxiliary modulator qubit, exploiting a Zeno-like mechanism to dynamically reshape the effective Hamiltonian and switch the charger-battery coupling. They analyze a minimal three-body model and extend to a collective many-body architecture, also discussing an NV-13C spin platform implementation.
result: The mechanism works beyond the ideal fast-control limit and preserves the collective charging power enhancement scaling with the number of battery units.
conclusion: Modulator-assisted Zeno control offers a scalable route to regulating energy transfer in quantum batteries, with potential experimental feasibility in spin platforms.

title: Quantum Nonlocality Without Entanglement And State Discrimination Measures
authors: Shayeef Murshid, Tathagata Gupta, Vincent Russo, And Somshubhro Bandyopadhyay
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2174 (2026).

An ensemble of product states is said to exhibit “quantum nonlocality without entanglement” if it cannot be optimally discriminated using local operations and classical communication (LOCC). We show that this property can depend on the chosen discrimination measure. Specifically, we construct a family of ensembles, each consisting of six linearly independent, equally probable bipartite product states, for which LOCC fails to achieve optimal minimum-error discrimination but succeeds in achieving optimal unambiguous discrimination. We further extend our construction to multipartite systems and provide strong numerical evidence that a similar separation between local and global optima is present for minimum-error discrimination, but not for unambiguous discrimination.

.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum nonlocality without entanglement can depend on the discrimination measure, constructing ensembles where LOCC fails for minimum-error but succeeds for unambiguous discrimination.
motivation: To understand whether the phenomenon of quantum nonlocality without entanglement is robust across different operational tasks of state discrimination.
method: Constructs explicit ensembles of six linearly independent, equally probable bipartite product states and analyzes their optimal discrimination under LOCC for both minimum-error and unambiguous discrimination measures, extending to multipartite systems with numerical evidence.
result: Demonstrates a separation: LOCC cannot achieve optimal minimum-error discrimination but can achieve optimal unambiguous discrimination for the constructed ensembles; similar separation is numerically indicated for multipartite systems.
conclusion: The property of quantum nonlocality without entanglement is measure-dependent, highlighting the importance of specifying the discrimination task when studying such phenomena.

title: Non-commutative Optimization Problems With Differential Constraints
authors: Mateus Araújo, Andrew J. P. Garner, And Miguel Navascues
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2169 (2026).

Non-commutative polynomial optimization (NPO) problems seek to minimize the state average of a polynomial of some operator variables, subject to polynomial constraints, over all states and operators, as well as the Hilbert spaces where those might be defined. Many of these problems are known to admit a complete hierarchy of semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations. In this work, we consider a variant of NPO problems where a subset of the operator variables satisfies a system of ordinary differential equations. We prove that, under mild conditions of operator boundedness, for every such problem one can construct a standard NPO problem with the same solution. This allows us to define a complete hierarchy of SDPs to tackle the original differential problem. We apply this method to bound averages of local observables in quantum spin systems subject to a Hamiltonian evolution (i.e., a quench). We find that, even in the thermodynamic limit of infinitely many sites, low levels of the hierarchy provide very good approximations for reasonably long evolution times.

.
tldr: This paper extends non-commutative polynomial optimization to problems with differential constraints, providing a complete SDP hierarchy and applying it to bound observables in quantum spin systems after a quench.
motivation: Many quantum information problems involve operator variables subject to differential equations, which are not directly solvable by standard NPO methods. The authors aim to bridge this gap by reducing such problems to standard NPO, enabling the use of existing SDP hierarchies.
method: The authors prove that under boundedness conditions, any NPO problem with differential constraints can be transformed into an equivalent standard NPO problem. This allows the construction of a complete hierarchy of SDP relaxations for the original problem.
result: The method is applied to bound local observables in quantum spin systems under Hamiltonian evolution, showing that low levels of the hierarchy yield good approximations even in the thermodynamic limit for reasonably long times.
conclusion: This work provides a new tool for analyzing quantum dynamics and optimization with differential constraints, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Mpc In The Quantum Head (or: Superposition-Secure (Quantum) Zero-Knowledge)
authors: Andrea Coladangelo, Ruta Jawale, Dakshita Khurana, Giulio Malavolta, And Hendrik Waldner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2161 (2026).

The MPC-in-the-head technique (Ishai et al., STOC 2007) is a celebrated method to build zero-knowledge protocols with desirable theoretical properties and high practical efficiency. This technique has generated a large body of research and has influenced the design of real-world post-quantum cryptographic signatures. In this work, we present a generalization of the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting, where the MPC is running a quantum computation. As an application of our framework, we propose a new approach to build zero-knowledge protocols where security holds even against a verifier that can obtain a superposition of transcripts. This notion was pioneered by Damgard et al., who built a zero-knowledge protocol for NP (in the common reference string model) secure against superposition attacks, by relying on perfectly hiding and unconditionally binding dual-mode commitments. Unfortunately, no such commitments are known from standard cryptographic assumptions. In this work we revisit this problem, and present two new three-round protocols in the common reference string model: (i) A zero-knowledge argument for NP, whose security reduces to the standard learning with errors (LWE) problem. (ii) A zero-knowledge argument for QMA from the same assumption.

.
tldr: This paper generalizes the MPC-in-the-head technique to the quantum setting, yielding zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks from standard LWE assumptions.
motivation: Existing zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks rely on dual-mode commitments not known from standard assumptions. The authors aim to construct such protocols from standard cryptographic assumptions.
method: They introduce a quantum generalization of MPC-in-the-head, where the MPC runs a quantum computation, and use it to build three-round zero-knowledge arguments for NP and QMA in the common reference string model.
result: They obtain two new protocols: one for NP and one for QMA, both secure against superposition attacks and based on the learning with errors (LWE) problem.
conclusion: This work provides a new framework for quantum zero-knowledge and demonstrates that superposition-secure zero-knowledge can be achieved from standard assumptions, advancing quantum cryptography.

title: From Superradiance To Superabsorption: An Exact Treatment Of Non-Markovian Cooperative Radiation
authors: Ignacio González And Ángel Rivas
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2159 (2026).

We investigate the emergence of cooperative radiation phenomena in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy resonant cavity beyond the Markovian and mean-field approximations. By deriving a complete analytical solution for the two-emitter case and employing a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, we characterize the full transition from Markovian to non-Markovian collective dynamics for systems of up to [MATH] emitters. Our results reveal three distinct regimes: a Markovian phase exhibiting the standard superradiant burst, a non-Markovian phase featuring spontaneous superabsorption of the emitted field, and a critical regime marked by pulsed collective emission. We show that the critical spectral width separating these behaviors increases monotonically with the number of emitters, demonstrating that environmental memory effects can be enhanced by cooperativity. Finally, we find that the superradiant scaling of the peak intensity progressively degrades with increasing system size, approaching a subquadratic law in the limit of a perfect cavity. In this regime, spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct manifestation of non-Markovian cooperativity.

.
tldr: This paper provides an exact treatment of non-Markovian cooperative radiation in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy cavity, revealing superabsorption and pulsed emission regimes.
motivation: To understand cooperative radiation beyond Markovian and mean-field approximations, which is crucial for quantum technologies involving atom-cavity systems.
method: Derives an analytical solution for two emitters and uses a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, characterizing the transition from Markovian to non-Markovian dynamics.
result: Identifies three regimes: Markovian superradiance, non-Markovian superabsorption, and critical pulsed emission; shows that the critical spectral width increases with emitter number and that superradiant scaling degrades with system size.
conclusion: Environmental memory effects can be enhanced by cooperativity, and spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct non-Markovian cooperative phenomenon.

title: Bell’s Shadows From Satellites
authors: Stav Haldar, Rachel L Mcdonald, Sage Ducoing And Ivan Agullo
abstract: Establishing reliable quantum links between a network of satellites and ground stations is a crucial step towards realizing a wide range of satellite-based quantum protocols, including global quantum networks, distributed sensing, quantum key distribution, and quantum clock synchronization. In this article, we envision a network of satellites and ground stations where quantum links are created through the exchange of entangled photon pairs. We simulate the dynamics of a satellite constellation and a set of Bell tests between the constellation and ground stations. We identify the regions on Earth where Bell tests can be successfully conducted with a satellite or a set of them, at a specified level of confidence. These regions move with the constellation and will be referred to as Bell violation shadows. We demonstrate that these shadows provide valuable insights for the study and evaluation of many satellite-mediated or satellite-assisted quantum protocols.
tldr: This paper simulates satellite constellations to identify moving regions on Earth where Bell tests can be successfully conducted, providing insights for satellite-based quantum protocols.
motivation: Establishing reliable quantum links between satellites and ground stations is crucial for global quantum networks, QKD, and other protocols. The authors aim to understand where and when Bell tests can be performed with satellite constellations.
method: They simulate the dynamics of a satellite constellation and ground stations, modeling the exchange of entangled photon pairs. They then identify regions on Earth where Bell tests can be conducted at a specified confidence level, calling these 'Bell violation shadows'.
result: The simulations reveal moving regions on Earth where Bell tests can be successfully conducted with one or more satellites, and these shadows provide insights for evaluating satellite-mediated quantum protocols.
conclusion: The concept of Bell violation shadows offers a valuable tool for planning and optimizing satellite-based quantum communication networks.

abstract:

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review analyzes information-theoretic approaches and proposed tabletop experiments for testing whether gravity induces entanglement, aiming to constrain theories of quantum gravity.
motivation: To address the fundamental question of whether gravity is quantum or classical by using information-theoretic methods, specifically gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) experiments.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and analyzes various proposed tabletop-scale GIE experiments, focusing on how quantum information concepts can be applied to test quantum gravity.
result: It provides a status update on theoretical approaches and concrete analyses of feasible GIE experiments, highlighting their potential to constrain new theories.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods, particularly GIE experiments, offer a promising path to empirically probe the quantum nature of gravity.
